source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Self-limited viral illness, because bruising and persistent abnormal blood counts are expected findings with routine viruses.","B":"Isolated orthopedic injury, because bone pain alone explains recurrent infections, fatigue, bruising, and blood-count changes.","C":"Leukemia, because marrow disease can present with fatigue, infection, bruising or bleeding, bone pain, and abnormal counts.","D":"Simple iron deficiency alone, because it routinely causes abnormal leukocyte proliferation, infections, and bone pain."}}
source_row.rationale: The combination of fatigue, bruising/bleeding, recurrent infection, bone pain and abnormal blood counts is concerning for leukemia because marrow disease disrupts normal hematopoiesis; diagnosis requires formal hematologic testing.
source_row.source_detail: Leukemia clinical evaluation material notes fatigue/weakness from anemia, infection, easy bruising/bleeding from marrow dysfunction and bone/joint pain as possible findings prompting hematologic evaluation. Official NCI SEER Training Modules current content rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client has fatigue, easy bruising, recurrent infections, bone pain and abnormal blood counts. Which disorder warrants prompt hematologic evaluation?
